title: Birla Planetarium | Kolkata Trips
description: Explore Birla Planetarium Kolkata with details on history, architecture, ticket price, show timings, how to reach, nearby attractions, and FAQs.
textContent: Birla Planetarium Standing beside the iconic Victoria Memorial on Jawaharlal Nehru Road, Birla Planetarium Kolkata is one of India’s oldest and largest planetariums. Since its inauguration in 1963, it has inspired millions of visitors with fascinating astronomy shows, celestial demonstrations, and educational programs. Popularly known as Taramandal, the planetarium combines science, education, and entertainment, making it one of the most visited attractions in Kolkata. Whether you are travelling with children, an astronomy enthusiast, or simply looking for an engaging indoor experience, Birla Planetarium deserves a place on your Kolkata itinerary. Overview of Birla Planetarium Kolkata Location: Jawaharlal Nehru Road (Chowringhee), Kolkata Established: 2 July 1963 Designed by: G. M. Bhuta & Associates Managed by: Birla Institute of Fundamental Research Known for: Astronomy shows, sky simulations, educational programs, telescope observations Popular Name: Taramandal For decades, the planetarium has served as an important centre for astronomy education, attracting students, researchers, families, and tourists from across India and abroad. History of Birla Planetarium Kolkata The idea of establishing a modern planetarium in Kolkata was envisioned by the renowned Birla family to promote scientific awareness and astronomy education. Construction began in the early 1960s, and the planetarium was inaugurated on 2 July 1963 by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru. At the time of its opening, it was the largest planetarium in Asia and among the largest in the world. Over the years, it has undergone several technological upgrades, transitioning from traditional mechanical projection systems to advanced digital projection technologies. Today, it continues to educate visitors through multilingual astronomy presentations and scientific exhibitions. Architecture and Design The architecture of Birla Planetarium is inspired by the famous Buddhist Stupa at Sanchi, giving it a distinctive white circular dome that has become one of Kolkata’s architectural landmarks. Architectural Highlights Massive hemispherical dome Circular auditorium with comfortable seating State-of-the-art digital projection systems Advanced sound technology Astronomical exhibits in the lobby Spacious landscaped surroundings The impressive dome offers an immersive experience, allowing visitors to virtually travel across galaxies, observe constellations, and witness astronomical phenomena. What to See Inside Birla Planetarium The main attraction is the immersive sky theatre where visitors experience realistic simulations of the night sky. Highlights include: Astronomy Shows Shows explain topics such as: Solar System Planets Stars Galaxies Black Holes Space Exploration Seasonal Night Sky Constellations Moon Missions Indian Astronomy Shows are available in multiple languages including: English Bengali Hindi Digital Projection System Modern projection technology creates: Realistic night skies Planetary movements Solar eclipses Meteor showers Deep-space journeys Galaxy simulations Astronomy Exhibits Visitors can also explore displays featuring: Astronomical instruments Space missions Models of planets Space exploration history Information panels on stars and galaxies Telescope Observation During special astronomical events and selected evenings, visitors may observe celestial objects using telescopes installed by the planetarium. Birla Planetarium Show Timings The planetarium conducts multiple shows every day in different languages. Typical schedule includes: English Shows Bengali Shows Hindi Shows Each show generally lasts 35–45 minutes. Schedules may vary depending on the day, season, educational events, or maintenance. It is advisable to check the latest timetable before visiting. Birla Planetarium Ticket Price Ticket prices are generally affordable. Typical categories include: Adults Children School Groups Educational Institutions Special rates are often available for educational visits. Prices are subject to revision. Best Time to Visit Birla Planetarium Kolkata The planetarium can be visited throughout the year. The most pleasant months are: October November December January February Since it is an indoor attraction, it is also an excellent option during Kolkata’s hot summer afternoons or monsoon season. Weekday mornings are usually less crowded than weekends and holidays. How to Reach Birla Planetarium The planetarium enjoys a central location in Kolkata. By Metro The nearest metro stations are: Maidan Rabindra Sadan Both stations are within walking distance. By Bus Numerous public and private buses operate along Jawaharlal Nehru Road. By Taxi Taxis and app-based cabs are readily available from all parts of Kolkata. By Train Howrah Railway Station: approximately 7 km Sealdah Railway Station: approximately 5 km By Air Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport is approximately 18 km away. Nearby Attractions A visit to Birla Planetarium can easily be combined with several nearby attractions. Victoria Memorial One of Kolkata’s most iconic monuments featuring museums, gardens, and colonial architecture. St. Paul’s Cathedral A beautiful Gothic cathedral known for its stained-glass windows and peaceful atmosphere. Maidan Kolkata’s vast green open space, perfect for leisurely walks and horse carriage rides. Indian Museum India’s oldest museum featuring archaeology, geology, zoology, and art collections. Why Visit Birla Planetarium? Visitors enjoy: Educational astronomy presentations Family-friendly environment Excellent rainy-day attraction Air-conditioned auditorium Modern digital projection Affordable tickets Suitable for children and adults Centrally located Easy accessibility One of India’s historic planetariums Visitor Tips Arrive at least 20–30 minutes before your scheduled show. Confirm the language of the show when purchasing tickets. Photography is generally restricted inside the auditorium. Mobile phones should remain on silent mode during presentations. Pair your visit with Victoria Memorial and St. Paul’s Cathedral for a rewarding half-day sightseeing experience. During weekends and school holidays, book tickets early to avoid long queues. Interesting Facts About Birla Planetarium Opened in 1963. One of the oldest planetariums in India. Inspired by the Sanchi Stupa. Initially the largest planetarium in Asia. Receives hundreds of thousands of visitors annually. Conducts astronomy education programmes for schools and colleges. Hosts special events during eclipses, meteor showers, and major astronomical occurrences. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 1. Where is Birla Planetarium Kolkata located? It is located on Jawaharlal Nehru Road beside Victoria Memorial in central Kolkata. 2. What is Birla Planetarium famous for? It is famous for its astronomy shows, digital sky projections, and educational space presentations. 3. How long does a show last? Most shows last approximately 35–45 minutes. 4. Are shows available in English? Yes. Shows are usually conducted in English, Bengali, and Hindi. 5. Is Birla Planetarium suitable for children? Yes. It is one of Kolkata’s best educational attractions for children and families. 6. Can photography be done inside? Photography is generally not permitted inside the planetarium auditorium during shows. 7. Which metro station is nearest? Maidan and Rabindra Sadan Metro Stations are the closest. 8. What is the best time to visit? October to February offers the most pleasant weather, though the indoor attraction can be enjoyed throughout the year. 9. Is parking available? Limited parking is available near the planetarium, though public transport is recommended during weekends. 10. Can school groups visit? Yes. The planetarium regularly hosts educational visits for schools and colleges. 11. Is Birla Planetarium wheelchair accessible? Most visitor areas are accessible, though it is advisable to confirm specific accessibility arrangements before visiting. 12. Can I combine Birla Planetarium with other attractions? Absolutely. It pairs well with Victoria Memorial, St. Paul’s Cathedral, the Maidan, and the Indian Museum, all located nearby. 13. How much time should I allocate for a visit? Plan for around 1.5 to 2 hours, including the show and time to explore the exhibits. 14. Does the planetarium host special events? Yes. It often organizes lectures, sky observation sessions, and special programmes during major astronomical events. 15. Why is Birla Planetarium one of Kolkata’s top attractions? Its unique blend of science, education, architecture, and immersive visual experiences makes it a must-visit destination for visitors of all ages.
